intro: Brushwork can record a gesture, define each edge, describe living things or let a landscape take over the page. Each picture puts the black line and empty paper to a different use.
alt: Four reinterpretations with large black brush gestures, meticulous color washes, birds and flowers, and a small figure in a mostly empty landscape.

variants.name: Chinese calligraphy
variants.look: Ink sweeps and dry edges draw a portrait through gesture alone.
variants.history: Chinese calligraphy encompasses distinct scripts and histories. In works like the calligraphy surrounding landscape paintings, variation in ink, pressure and speed is visible in actual written characters.
variants.when: Work with a calligrapher when written words and physical brush movement both matter.
variants.why: Pressure, direction and ink load make the movement of the brush visible.

variants.name: gongbi painting
variants.look: Fine outlines and thin washes define every fold and strand.
variants.history: Gongbi refers to painstaking brushwork. It has been used to achieve close description in figures, court painting and bird-and-flower subjects.
variants.when: Paint a close subject with details small enough to reward repeated viewing.
variants.why: A steady contour can keep the smallest forms clear beneath several transparent layers.

source.label: Tsinghua University Art Museum | Chinese painting exhibition

variants.name: bird-and-flower painting
variants.look: Birds and flowering branches fill the composition around a small portrait.
variants.history: Bird-and-flower painting became an established subject by the Song period. Plants, birds and insects can show close observation and also carry seasonal or symbolic associations.
variants.when: Give a portrait a clear season through plants and animal behavior.
variants.why: Accurately chosen species and colored forms add meaning while retaining an observational scale.

source.label: Museum of Asian Art, Berlin | Ducks in the Lotus Pond

variants.name: literati painting
variants.look: A small outline figure sits under faint mountains on an open expanse of paper.
variants.history: Chinese scholar-artists developed painting practices in which brushwork, poetry and landscape expressed personal cultivation. Chinese literati landscape often uses emptiness to suggest distance.
variants.when: Set the figure into a landscape where the weather and distance must carry the mood.
variants.why: Sparse marks let apparently empty paper read as air, water or a pause in the picture.

source.label: The Met | Landscape painting in Chinese art

prompt: Make one square image with four independently composed equal-size square artworks in an exact 2x2 grid, precise split on each midpoint, full bleed with no gutters. Four artworks, each uses brush stylistically in a different way. The heroine with glasses, low bun and mug should be present in each.. The attached portrait is just a character reference. Our character is a 30-year-old woman with light ash-blonde hair in a neat low bun, black rectangular glasses always visible, tailored charcoal knee-length sheath dress and fitted blazer with an azure pocket square, blue lanyard, little four-color windowpane clip when feasible. She holds a signature white coffee mug. Freeze identity, repeat the subject in every distinct art idiom. Copy no reference card composition or type. No writing, digits, words or labels; no diptych or pastiche. top left: Forceful abstract Chinese brushwork, calligraphic broad central gesture without letters, calligraphic energy resolved into expressive sparse silhouette, monochrome blacks and ink splashes on creamy white plain paper. top right: Meticulous gongbi brush painting, measured fine ink contours, layered thin color washes and delicate detail in hair, skin and crisp dress pleats. bottom left: Bird-and-flower brush painting with meticulous luminous peonies, blossoms, and jewel-colored small birds occupying most of the composition, and a small recognizable bust of executive centered amidst the foliage. bottom right: Chinese literati ink landscape with very small outline figure holding cup in a vast airy ink landscape, dry strokes and choppy distant mountain wash, minimal colors and large blank areas.
